summary: A plain-object value given to .default()/.prefault() is cloned on each parse instead of the same object instance being returned every time.

.extend() on an object schema that carries refinements throws instead of silently dropping the refinements (narrowed in 4.3.1 to throw only when an existing key is overwritten; .safeExtend() is the supported path).
z.uuid() accepts the all-F 'Max UUID' (FFFFFFFF-FFFF-FFFF-FFFF-FFFFFFFFFFFF) that it previously rejected.
The inferred output type of z.promise(T) is Promise<output<T>> instead of the unwrapped output<T> (z.promise() was already deprecated).
.pick() and .omit() on an object schema that carries refinements throw instead of silently dropping the refinements.

The mask given to .pick()/.omit()/.partial()/.required() (and the Zod Mini functions) is a TypeScript error when it names a key not in the shape; such keys previously type-checked, though the runtime already threw.
z.e164() requires a non-zero leading digit and 7-15 digits in total, rejecting some phone strings it accepted before.
Registering a schema under an id already in a registry overwrites silently instead of throwing; duplicate ids are instead rejected by z.toJSONSchema().
A type-predicate function passed to .refine() narrows the schema's output type; previously the predicate was ignored and the output type was unchanged.
An intersection that includes z.strictObject() rejects only keys unrecognized by both sides; previously a key unknown to either side failed the parse.
Zod Mini schemas no longer expose a .refine() method; use .check(z.refine(fn)) instead.

Tuple parsing writes element defaults into the output (filling positions before a defaulted element with undefined); previously defaults in tuple positions were not materialized, and tuple-length errors, including z.function() argument errors, changed shape.
Object properties typed z.undefined(), z.any() or z.unknown() require the key to be present at parse time (the value may be undefined); Zod 4.0-4.3 accepted a missing key.
.merge() throws when the receiving object schema has refinements instead of producing ambiguous refinement behavior; refinements on the argument schema are kept.

z.toJSONSchema() output changes in four places: no redundant id inside $defs entries, different min/max for intersections under the draft-04 and openapi-3.0 targets, a recursive z.lazy() with .describe() converts instead of overflowing the stack, and falsy prefault values (0, '', false) are emitted as default where they were omitted.

Three string formats are stricter: z.base64() rejects whitespace it used to tolerate, z.cuid() accepts only c plus at least 6 base36 characters (its JSON Schema pattern follows) instead of any 8 or more non-space, non-hyphen characters, and z.httpUrl() rejects a single slash after the scheme (https:/example.com) that the URL constructor used to repair.
z.cuid(), the .cuid() chain method and the related CUID v1 classes and regex export are marked @deprecated in favor of z.cuid2().

ZodError output for unions changes: z.treeifyError() and z.formatError() keep the full path of issues nested inside unions, and invalid-discriminator issues from z.discriminatedUnion() carry the discriminator options and a reworded message.
z.discriminatedUnion() option schemas must have the discriminator key in their input type; options that lack it are now TypeScript errors.
z.iso.datetime() (with or without offset: true) rejects minute-precision input such as 2020-01-01T06:15Z that it accepted before; local: true still allows it.
String .min()/.max()/.length() count Unicode code points instead of UTF-16 code units, so astral characters such as emoji count once.
A record's key schema governs only keys that match it, so intersecting an object with a pattern-keyed record no longer rejects the object's own keys as invalid_key.
An unrecognized_keys issue no longer aborts the object it came from, so a strict object with an extra key and a bad value reports both issues instead of the first alone.
Object and record parsers always drop a __proto__ key (from input, schema or key transform), and .strict() reports an own __proto__ input key as unrecognized_keys instead of swallowing it.

Several string formats are stricter: z.ipv6() checks the address alphabet directly instead of via new URL() (rejecting ::1 followed by a newline), z.ulid() requires a first character of 0-7, z.httpUrl() enforces the RFC 1035 host length limits, the z.emoji() regex no longer backtracks exponentially, and the JSON Schema pattern for .includes(sub, { position: N }) allows at least N leading characters instead of exactly N.

ZodNumberFormat takes a format type parameter so ZodInt, ZodFloat32, ZodFloat64, ZodInt32 and ZodUInt32 (and the bigint formats) are distinct at the type level instead of one interchangeable type (commit marked with !).
The ZodError produced by .safeParse() no longer captures a stack trace at construction, so result.error.stack is not the call site it used to be.

z.toJSONSchema() behaves differently for inputs it already handled: a root schema with an id in its metadata is emitted as a root $ref into $defs, a union of simple primitive types becomes a type array instead of anyOf, and the override callback runs before the unrepresentable error is thrown.
.safeParse() builds its ZodError lazily, so error maps (global, locale and per-schema error) run when result.error is first read rather than at parse time.
z.emoji() rejects strings made only of emoji components (digits, #, *, lone modifiers or joiners) such as "123" that it previously accepted.
z.enum(NumericEnum).options lists only the numeric values; the reverse-mapping member names that it used to include (and that failed to parse) are gone.

The runtime regexes behind z.base64()/z.base64url() check only the alphabet with length and padding enforced in code (z.regexes.base64url becomes the length-aware form), and the z.email() pattern (z.regexes.email, issue.pattern and the JSON Schema pattern) drops its lookaheads and capture groups; composing either into a template literal no longer applies the dropped rules to the rest of the string.
z.toJSONSchema() folds chained checks as a conjunction, so a later format check no longer overwrites tighter min/max bounds and repeated multipleOf or min/length chains emit the correct constraints.

Schema members .format, .minLength, .maxLength, .minValue, .maxValue, .isInt, .minDate and .maxDate are prototype getters materialized on first read (absent from Object.keys until then) and report the tightest bound rather than the last-written one.
